newsitem.title: USA: MCI to cut stake in ASkyB venture.
newsitem.headline: MCI to cut stake in ASkyB venture.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said on Sunday that it was redefining its relationship with News Corp and would cut its stake in the direct broadcasting satellite venture, ASkyB, to around 20 percent from 50 percent.
"We are in the process of defining our relationship with News Corp," Bert Roberts, MCI chief executive, told a news conference on the company's $20 billion merger with British Telecommunications Plc.
Roberts said that the overall media venture with News Corp would not directly be affected by MCI's merger with BT, but was being reexamined.
News Corp had agreed to the cut in the stake in ASkyB, Roberts said.
Roberts said that News Corp's concentration on the consumer market and MCI's focus on the business market was the main reason for MCI cutting its stake.
"We will get reimbursed...It will be more of a passive relationship (with News Corp's satellite service)," Roberts said.
Roberts said that they would now be seeking more partners to pick up the remaining 30 percent or so in ASkyB.

MCI in 1995 agreed to a wide-ranging $1 billion media venture with News Corp. As part of the link to Rupert Murdoch's media empire, MCI took options to build a stake of up to 13 percent in News Corp itself.
Analysts said at the time that they could see little overlap between MCI's blue chip-business customers and News Corp's blue collar media and newspaper expertise.

Analysts also noted that although MCI bought the last available satellite slot above the U.S. for the ASkyB venture, it is still running at least a year behind some of its rivals, including AT&T Corp, which has a stake in Hughes Electronics Corp's DirectTV.
